content.title: About
content.content: Black Forest cake (Schwarzwälder Kirschtorte) is a classic German dessert made of chocolate sponge, layers of cherries, whipped cream, and chocolate shavings. The cupcake version keeps the same flavor profile in a convenient single‑serve form.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The cake is named after the Black Forest region, where traditionally the cherries were harvested.
The original recipe uses Kirsch, a cherry brandy that gives the cake its distinctive aroma.
Typical decoration includes chocolate curls and whole cherries, creating a contrast between dark chocolate and bright fruit.
In the United States the Black Forest flavor is often offered as cupcakes, which are easier to transport and store.
There are many variations, including alcohol‑free versions that omit the Kirsch.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Cherries contain anthocyanins that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Fresh cherries and cream provide vitamin C, supporting the immune system.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Cherries and whole‑grain sponge add fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Calcium from cream
items.content: Whipped cream supplies calcium, important for bone health.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: The combination of carbs and fats offers a quick source of energy.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Black Forest cake and cupcakes contain a lot of sugar, which can be problematic for people with diabetes.

items.title: Allergy to nuts and dairy
items.content: Recipes often include almonds and cream, which may trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Alcohol in kirsch
items.content: Traditional kirsch contains alcohol; consider this when serving to children or abstaining guests.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Chocolate, cream, and sugar make the dessert calorie‑rich, so portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the cake chilled, sliced into portions. Cupcakes are eaten by hand and are ideal for picnics or office snacks. Add fresh cherries on top or sprinkle extra chocolate shavings for extra flair.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cake refrigerated, covered with plastic wrap, for up to 3 days. Cupcakes can be stored in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days or in the fridge for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze in freezer‑safe bags and thaw in the refrigerator before serving.
